key_insight: High-resolution hurricane LES captures materially different turbulent inflow structures, which can substantially change the predicted loads and aeroelastic response of an idling wind turbine.
engineering_relevance: Accurate extreme-wind design for turbines in tropical-cyclone-prone regions depends on using sufficiently resolved inflow fields rather than coarse storm representations.
method: LES of Hurricane Laura at three grid spacings: 55.55 m, 25 m, and 10 m
Used simulated hurricane inflow directly as boundary conditions for aeroelastic turbine simulations
Compared mean wind and turbulence structure evolution as the storm passed a virtual turbine site
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant differences in mean wind and turbulence across grid resolutions, producing distinct turbine aeroelastic responses in the coupled simulations.
watch_item: Results are based on one hurricane case and one virtual turbine location, so broader design use needs additional storms, locations, and validation.
paper_title: Hurricane Laura-induced loads on wind turbines -- Part I: High-fidelity modeling and sensitivity to turbulent inflow conditions
